# Research: Orchestrator issue requirements, conflicts and dependencies

**Investigation type:** Doc Analyst  
**Scope:** Issues #339, #423, #431, #409, #326 and #446; PRs #422 and #449; current worker contract, ownership hook and relevant implementation; prior #444 analyses.  
**Status:** Complete  
**Date:** 2026-11-09  
**Delivery:** Findings returned directly, as requested. No report file written.

## 1. Evidence and interpretation

The issues describe three distinct concerns: session supervision, cross-workspace knowledge sharing, and delegated supervision. They do not establish that these must ship together.

### Evidence tags

- **[CODE-VERIFIED]** means the cited source was read. For instruction-based components, it establishes the shipped instruction or test—not proof that every session obeys it.
- **[CODE-CONTRADICTED]** means current source contradicts the documentation claim.
- **[UNVERIFIED]** means a proposal is not implemented in the inspected surfaces, a runtime claim was not reproduced, or the relevant enforcement path was not established.
- **[GH-OBSERVED]** identifies issue/PR text or state read directly from GitHub. It does not establish implementation.

- The current contract and its phrase tests are inspectable; successful runtime supervision is a separate claim.

## 2. Every requirement in #339, classified

### Comment references

All five comments returned for [#339](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/339) were read.

| Reference | Comment |
|---|---|
| C1 | [Polling, cleanup and “Version 2” hierarchy](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/339#issuecomment-6659516712) |
| C2 | [Permission-mode incident and security design sketch](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/339#issuecomment-6659559030) |
| C3 | [Research questions and adversarial library choice](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/339#issuecomment-6703399956) |
| C4 | [Historical accuracy check](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/339#issuecomment-6703934716) |
| C5 | [Claim summary and proposed first step](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/339#issuecomment-6703934983) |

**Classification:** “V1-independent” means the requirement concerns an orchestrator even without sub-orchestrators. It does **not** move security work that C2 explicitly schedules for a later release into v1. “Sub-only” means it specifically requires a delegated supervisory layer.

**Key Takeaways**

- Most #339 requirements apply without a middle layer.
- Fixed messages and single-level grants do not inherently require sub-orchestrators, but C2 explicitly places their build in its later security release.
- Delegated narrowing, supervisory child ownership and confirmation-free hierarchical operation are the genuinely sub-specific requirements.

## 3. Requirements versus the shipped contract

| Conflict | Evidence | Consequence for the decision |
|---|---|---|
| A slash command that directly performs Orca coordination versus “Commands themselves contain no Orca calls.” | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:5 and 40 states the restriction. **[CODE-CONTRADICTED]** As a universal description of current implementation, the claim is too broad: ISSUE-CODE:666–682 runs worktree creation and 1351–1355 launches an agent. | A future orchestration command needs an explicit architectural boundary or exception. Existing coordinator-only `/sc:issue` behavior is precedent to examine—not blanket permission to discard WC-8. |
| Supervised sub-orchestrator with helpers versus worker-session fan-out prohibition. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:62 prohibits worker-start, dispatch, task creation and alternate agent/worktree launches at any depth setting. | O3 cannot be enabled just by adding a flag or raising depth. WC-13 and its review/test surfaces must change. |
| Agent-launched coordinator versus person-opened coordinator definition. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:69; CORE:55–59 names a coordinator under another orchestrator while preserving worker-contract precedence. | The wording names a role without defining its supervision, authority or lifecycle. It does not authorize workers to create worktrees. |
| “All sessions through orchestrator” versus human-only decisions. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:57, 232 and 250–269. | Rulings, frozen worktrees and PR-session ownership remain separate. A second coordinator cannot provide human approval. |
| Broad token authorization versus current outward-action ownership. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:41 says no brief can enable worker outward actions; 229 requires the person’s named instruction; 233 requires review before publishing unseen worker commits. | A signed token does not by itself satisfy the current policy. Authority policy must be settled before choosing token syntax. |
| Automatic cleanup versus protected state. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:225 and 250–253 protect unread reports, unfinished ledgers and frozen worktrees. | “Done” and “safe to delete” are distinct decisions at either one or two supervisory levels. |
| Disposable plans/reports versus retained task evidence. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:234 stages task material; 225 protects unread reports. | The original blanket artifact exclusion must not become cleanup logic. |
| Worktree per prompt versus conditional placement. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:47, 220–225. | Worktree hierarchy is placement, not proof of supervisory hierarchy. |
| Proposed six message types versus existing lifecycle vocabulary and identity checks. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:101, 105–108; SEND-CODE:33–65. | Separate application requests from Orca lifecycle messages. Do not manufacture child completion messages or acknowledge foreign messages indiscriminately. |
| Timeout-based recovery versus positive settlement proof. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:46, 73–79, 157–192. | More supervisors must not create more independent restart authorities. |
| Cross-workspace course corrections versus ownership and pull-based follow-ups. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:61 and 246. **[UNVERIFIED]** A cross-coordinator correction/admission protocol was not established. | #423 may share knowledge without granting another orchestrator control of someone else’s Tasks. |
| Replacing response summaries versus the current output style. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** STYLE:22. | The report requirement needs an explicit exception or compatible presentation rule, irrespective of sub mode. |

### Hook behavior is narrower than ownership policy

**[CODE-VERIFIED]** HOOK’s `track(o,w)` records the agent/help flags and positional words. `fin(o)` blocks a recognized worktree create missing both the agent and help flags. The final script reads Bash command text, runs that scanner and returns the block message.

There is no coordinator/worker role input to that decision. Consequently:

- **[CODE-VERIFIED]** It enforces a syntactic agent requirement for the commands it recognizes.
- **[CODE-CONTRADICTED]** Treating it as an authority-aware WC-13 enforcement mechanism would be incorrect.
- **[UNVERIFIED]** It establishes neither safe delegation nor ownership enforcement outside its recognized Bash path.

**Key Takeaways**

- The most immediate conflict exists even for v1: a command whose purpose is Orca coordination meets a contract written to keep ordinary commands Orca-free.
- CORE’s middle-layer wording is not a complete sub-orchestrator contract.
- Raising depth cannot replace policy, identity, admission and cleanup rules.

## 4. The “v2” naming collision

| Source | Exact wording | Meaning supported by the text |
|---|---|---|
| #339 C1 | “Version 2 should include an orchestrator of orchestrators.” | **[UNVERIFIED proposal]** Hierarchical supervision. |
| #339 C2 | “For the orchestrator-of-orchestrators in version 2, the top Orchestrator grants a sub-orchestrator a token for its set of worktrees; the sub-orchestrator can only narrow it further for its children.” | **[UNVERIFIED proposal]** Delegated, attenuated authority. |
| #339 C2 recommendation | “Build Steps 2 and 3 as part of version 2, before any orchestrator-of-orchestrators work.” | **[UNVERIFIED proposal]** Typed messages and grants precede hierarchy. |
| [#423](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/423), Feature Summary | “Orchestrator v2 - Proactive Holistic” gives each Orchestrator “a catalogue and working knowledge of what all agents across all workspaces are doing.” | **[UNVERIFIED proposal]** Cross-agent knowledge and course correction. |
| #423, Proposed Solution | “Treat this as v2, a separate future release after completion of the v1 orchestrator (#339), not an expansion of the v1 delivery scope.” | **[UNVERIFIED proposal]** Separate release sequencing, not a delegated-supervision design. |

**Resolution:** “v2” is an overloaded release label, not evidence that these scopes are identical. #423’s acceptance criteria cover catalogue refresh, relevance assessment, shared research and lessons, duplicate/overlapping work and course corrections. They do **not** specify sub-orchestrator creation, depth, narrowing grants, upward reporting or delegated cleanup authority.

For this decision, distinguish:

1. **V1 supervision — #339.**
2. **Proactive knowledge sharing — #423.**
3. **Hierarchical supervision and delegated authority — #339 C1/C2 plus this sub-orchestrator evaluation.**

**[UNVERIFIED]** No issue amendment or implemented release contract was found that resolves the naming administratively. The distinction above resolves interpretation, not ownership of a future release number.

**Key Takeaways**

- Implementing #423’s stated acceptance criteria would not implement #339’s hierarchy sketch.
- Neither knowledge sharing nor the plural “Each Orchestrator” proves a parent-child relationship.
- Do not use “v2 complete” as acceptance for sub mode without separate criteria.

## 5. What the related issues and PRs contribute

### 5.1 #431: liveness is already a v1 concern

[#431](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/431) reports eight failures: unchanged timer heartbeats during compact thrashing; idle prompts mistaken for work; one-file activity mistaken for liveness; a closing report hidden by message filters; answers sent but apparently not read; a permission prompt; stopping between chain steps; and repeated context exhaustion.

**[UNVERIFIED]** Those historical incidents were not reproduced. They are issue evidence, not newly observed runtime results.

| Issue requirement | Current source comparison | Bearing on a middle layer |
|---|---|---|
| Detect stalled, idle, blocked and unreachable workers within bounded time. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:110–129 defines semantic progress, deadlines and named states. | A proposed sub-orchestrator must itself be supervised, not merely relay child heartbeat counts. |
| See closing reports regardless of the type originally used. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:101 listens to all listed types; 108 recognizes suspicious completion-like status; 59 still requires actual completion through `worker_done`. | A parent must distinguish a supervisor’s progress from settlement of its children. |
| Confirm that an answer was read/applied rather than merely sent. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:58, 61 and 131–138 defines acknowledgements and pending-ack handling. | A relay needs acknowledgement at each boundary; receipt at the middle session is not proof of application by a child. |
| Avoid context thrashing and accidental turn endings. | **[CODE-VERIFIED]** WC:63–65 and 124 specifies chain continuity, bounded reading and handoff behavior. | A stalled middle session could leave live children without an effective supervisor; this is a design risk, **[UNVERIFIED]** in runtime. |
| Design richer progress/terminal/transcript signals and feed the result into #423. | **[UNVERIFIED proposal]** The issue asks for design first. | Do not confuse current instruction-based v1 rules with a completed autonomous monitor. |

The strongest existing caution is WC:200: whether two consumers on one mailbox both get a batch remains explicitly unverified; the coordinator therefore runs one waiter per Run inbox.

**Key Takeaways**

- #431 is not a reason to require hierarchy; its failures occur with one coordinator.
- Current shipped liveness instructions are materially newer than #339’s historical accuracy check.
- A hierarchy adds a new ownership and failure boundary that the current one-waiter rule does not resolve.

### 5.2 #446: bounded lock handling, not delegated Git authority

[#446](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/446) requests:

- Recheck an existing index lock after 1, 2, 3 and 4 seconds—about ten seconds total.
- Never delete, move or edit it.
- If it remains, report blocked with its path and modification-time age.
- Pin these conditions in the contract tests.
- Do not expand the wait to cover long commit hooks or assume changing a caller’s environment alters Orca’s runtime Git environment.

**[CODE-CONTRADICTED]** The requested retry is not yet in WC:45, which still says to report blocked with the path. Its cited line 44 is stale; the sentence is at line 45.

**[UNVERIFIED]** The issue’s throwaway-repository experiments and environment claim were not rerun here.

For a middle layer, this means a short wait may reduce false blocks, but it does not grant the middle session permission to remove locks, stage work, merge or override freezes. WC:41–45 and 229–234 still own those decisions.

**Key Takeaways**

- #446 is useful independently of `--sub`.
- It touches the same contract/test surfaces a hierarchy change would touch.
- Lock age is evidence for escalation, not authority to delete a lock.

### 5.3 #409: several orchestrators do not imply nested orchestrators

[#409](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/409) explicitly describes:

> “One human supervising 5-10 orchestrators and 50-100 sessions/worktrees…”

It also says the companion is:

> “not … a scheduler, or a session manager.”

Its out-of-scope list excludes approving, retrying, terminating, spawning, merging, rebasing, deleting worktrees and instructing workers.

**[UNVERIFIED proposal]** Its observer should display attention, scope, meaningful changes and evidence freshness, while keeping lifecycle, reports, acceptance, tests and human approval distinct. Its scenarios include uneven ownership and shared/unmapped worktrees; one-to-one session/worktree mapping is expressly not assumed.

The referenced local prototype directory was absent from this checkout. **[UNVERIFIED]** The published package, reported test results, version pins, live collection coverage and dashboard integration were not verified from source here. The issue itself calls its data synthetic and its source schema proposed.

**Decision implication:** #409 supports O2’s premise of multiple human-opened coordinators just as well as a future hierarchy. It does not require a middle layer, provide one, or authorize operational controls.

**Key Takeaways**

- #409 is an observation requirement, not a supervisory authority requirement.
- It provides useful evidence/display distinctions for v1 and later work.
- Do not import synthetic dashboard fields as an established Orca API contract.

### 5.4 #326: Git ownership limits survive the addition of another coordinator

[#326](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/326) initially proposes a central Git relay, regular commits, experiment worktrees, cleanup, submodules and improved GitHub communication.

Its [later approved-contract comment](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/326#issuecomment-6590983517) explicitly says:

> “D5: Orca’s nesting depth stays at 1.”

and:

Reopen O3/O4 only after the D5 evidence gate, transport-validation findings, delegated-authority policy, mailbox routing, liveness ownership and cleanup/freeze behavior are established.

The principal demonstrated benefit of O3 in D5 is avoiding a coordinator round trip for work whose split becomes known during execution. **[UNVERIFIED]** This assignment did not find measured evidence that this benefit outweighs another supervisor and authority boundary.

**Key Takeaways**

- Do not interpret deferral as rejection of parallelism.
- The issue sources support keeping hierarchy as an explicit future decision.
- No evidence here justifies changing nesting or permission settings now.

## Summary

Most #339 requirements—supervision, recovery, attention reporting and safe cleanup—apply without a sub-orchestrator. Its hierarchy sketch is explicitly later work preceded by transport research, typed messages and scoped grants, while #423’s “v2” describes a separate knowledge-sharing release rather than nested supervision. The current contract prohibits worker fan-out and retains person-only authority, even though #449 names a coordinator under another orchestrator; its hook verifies an agent flag, not delegated authority. Defer a new sub mode while retaining the two-tier contract, and use explicit evidence gates to revisit hierarchy rather than treating a launch path or release label as approval.

**Recommended next action:** Record the three separate scopes and the unresolved authority/routing gates in the research synthesis; this prevents the v1 release, #423 and sub mode from acquiring contradictory acceptance criteria.
